9.original: [... as he gives the victory to]
9.content: ... as he gives the victory to

spiritual_reading:
There is a full order of complete discernments from the Divine, sufficient for all states and all processes. These discernments proceed from the highest Divine degree and enter into the created domain to set all things into their true arrangement. Each discernment is appointed to its own use according to the will of the one Divine Discerner, who is above every particular discernment; this is the Divine Itself as the source of all love and all wisdom.

The first discernment is the primal power of good that first engaged evil and brought it low. It exposed and rejected the arrogance of the ruling falsity at the beginning, because that falsity had lifted itself up against a dominion of good that was not its own.

The second discernment is the living operation of Divine truth proceeding, which came to sustain what had been assaulted. It judged all the powers of evil that had violated the outer forms by which the primal good could act and be seen.

The third discernment is the wisdom-principle that proceeds from Divine love, which arranged the higher spiritual degree of the universe into beauty and order according to the Divine delight. It judged the dominant evils in the higher region, restraining them and fixing them in the state that matches what they have made themselves.

The fourth discernment is the formative Divine operation that establishes a new state of blessedness. It made a righteous judgement upon the hidden interiors of the adversary, so that spiritual death might no longer rise up as it had. It set a fixed restraint for evil. And at the highest point of that new formation it established a governing union for the primal good and for all who are in the origin of heavenly truth, those who entered combat with evil and overcame it.

The fifth discernment is the Divine rule of honor, abiding in the full completion of the highest outward spiritual degree. It is the discerner of all outward degrees, giving true judgement—righteous judgement—upon every power and every dominion that operates in outward appearances.

The sixth discernment is the proceeding Divine presence that mediates between the highest and the lower. It came and made the Divine likeness manifest. It purified the good of wisdom that had been mixed and obscured, distinguishing what is from the Divine from what had been seized and defiled by the adversary; the remainder of this action is unclear in the fragment, but the sense is that it completed a work of cleansing and restoration by separation.

The seventh discernment concerns the ordering of the domains of life by the laws of spiritual combat. It grants victory to those who remain firm in good and truth; it condemns those shown to be in confirmed evil and falsity. For the steadfast it becomes the ordered progression of advance; but the convicted it drives away and consigns to the lowest state, far from heavenly influx. This portion is partially lost, and some details of its mode are uncertain.

The eighth discernment is the Divine enlightening presence that teaches and leads all who are sent to proclaim truth. After the mediating Divine presence had made the Divine likeness manifest and the purified good of wisdom had been received, evils and falsities surged from interior and exterior levels to resist. Therefore this enlightening presence was sent. It descended into the outward degrees and executed judgement there, separating those who were constant in good from those who were convicted of evil.

The ninth discernment is the purity of heavenly truth in its receptive form, which by manifested holiness draws the inmost affections of the opposed powers, gathering what is its own into union. It judges the dominion of falsity that flows and persuades, and the dominion of falsity hardened into resistance.

The tenth discernment is the Divine scrutiny present in the intermediate region between inner and outer life, judging the human race in their general states. It separates those who are in good from those who are in evil, setting the just apart from those who live in sin.

The eleventh discernment is the enlightened understanding from heaven that will be manifested within the human state. It chooses the holy community of those who live from love and truth, it unveils what has been hidden, and it separates wisdom from falsity, and sets genuine truth apart from lawlessness.

The twelfth discernment is the great ordering counsel: the call to use and the obedience of reception, appointed in the most external fundamentals of life. It performs the final separation between the good and the evil. And at the end it can gather all things into a last, complete form, bringing the whole into a final, fixed order; and it separates wisdom from falsity.

These are the complete set of great discernments sent forth. They proceed from the one Divine Discerner who is above every particular discerning. He is the hidden and immeasurable Divine source, the One who is, established in eternal degrees upon the supreme governing union of Divine order and honor, ruling by Divine love within Divine wisdom.

fills.notes: The Mother of Life ‘beautifies and sets up’ the heavenly part; in the substrate this ordering is not self-originating but proceeds by commission from the higher Greatness. The verb must express delegated appointment: her formative delight operates within what has been given to her.

The Ambassador’s work here is discrimination and cleansing: the light is described as not simply defiled but mixed, i.e., good bound together with what is alien. This matches the correspondential sense: truth-wisdom obscured by admixture, requiring separation.

The clause must distinguish what belongs to him from what belongs to the enemy. In the oldest cosmological register this is expressed as seizure or capture: the enemy ‘took hold’ of light. Thus: the purified light is that which his own image had seized (recovered) as against what remained with the enemy.

The line closes the purification by an act of division: separating what is his own from what is the enemy’s. This is the required correspondential operation (discernment by discrete degrees), and it fits the fragment’s sense that ‘he has …’ completed a cleansing by separation.

fills.fill: as he gives the victory to
fills.notes: Retained: it exactly matches the substrate function of this judge as the law of combat that confirms the steadfast and grants victory.

fills.fill: in their works; for the steadfast
fills.notes: The surviving structure demands a balancing: he condemns those convicted (in their deeds), but for the steadfast he becomes ‘steps of the way’. Filling with an impersonal criterion (‘works’) keeps the oldest register (cosmic order by effects) rather than moral exhortation.

The narrative needs the transition: after the light was taken up, a mass of rulers rose up. This is the natural-sequence marker demanded by the spiritual sense (purified good received, then resistance surges).
Retained: this is a technical correspondential expression for drawing in the inmost affection or will of opposing powers by the manifest image, enabling the gathering of what is her own into her.

The Light Mind ‘unveils’ what corresponds to interiors previously covered. The oldest layer prefers a plain cosmological term (‘hidden things’) over later ecclesial or revelatory phrasing; it matches the subsequent separations (light from darkness, truth from lawlessness).

The closing identifies the throne of honour as ‘the King of Honour … in his kingdom’. The missing predicate must express rulership rather than naming another hypostasis: the Father is established upon that throne, which is the King of Honour reigning in his kingdom.

assessment: Most lacunae can be restored at the level of function: the missing pieces consistently describe delegated ordering (¶5), purification by discrimination and separation (¶8), judgement by confirmation or expulsion according to works (¶9), the sequence ‘light taken up → resistance’ (¶10), unveiling of interiors (¶13), and final enthroned rule (¶15). Exact verbal forms remain uncertain in ¶8–9 and ¶15 because the fragment preserves only the action-type, not fixed wording.
